audit.whatIsWrong: Defiant Dance is described nowhere, and dontsFull[1].t warns the reader off wasting charm on 'a shielded window'.
audit.why: Defiant Dance reduces PHYSICAL damage during the charge. Ahri deals magic damage, and her Q return is true damage — none of it is reduced. The page tells an Ahri player to respect a defensive window that does literally nothing against her, which costs her free poke every time Irelia charges W.
audit.corrected: dontsFull[1] retitled and rewritten: 'Defiant Dance reduces physical damage only — your orb, Fox-Fire and Charm all land in full through it.' The same fact carries tradeGood.
sources: brief.enemyKit W text ('She takes reduced physical damage during the charge')
brief.ownerKit Q text (magic out, true damage back)

audit.whatIsWrong: Six of seven level-chart rows disagree between layers. The full layer reads Irelia/Irelia/Irelia/Irelia/Skill/Skill/Skill; the content layer reads Skill/Skill/Skill/Irelia/Ahri/Ahri/Skill. The full layer also rates the first four rows 7/10 on the strength of the wrong side.
audit.why: The packet levelChart matches the content layer exactly. The full layer hands Irelia levels 1-3 — a stretch where she has 600 range and no stun until level 2-3 while Ahri orbs from 970 — and then denies Ahri the level 6 row the content layer explicitly gives her.
audit.corrected: phases[0..2].side -> Skill, phases[3].side -> Irelia, phases[4].side and phases[5].side -> Ahri, with phases[0..2].rating dropped from 7/10 to 5/10 to match a Skill row. Proposed as one atomic group.

audit.whatIsWrong: Nothing states that Charm stops Bladesurge, or how the Bladesurge reset actually works.
audit.why: Bladesurge is a 600-range dash that refreshes its cooldown if the target is Marked or dies to it, and it heals her. So the reset chain is the threat, Charm is the mechanical answer (it 'instantly stops movement abilities'), and a thin wave is what starves the reset. All three are absent.
audit.corrected: Written into winCon, tldr, breakdown.carry, ahead, dosFull[0].d and tradeBad.

audit.whatIsWrong: Difficulty is TRICKY 7/10 justified only as 'turning your every misstep into the all-in you hadn't budgeted', and the full layer calls Irelia 'he/his' in tldr, tradeGood, tradeBad and three dontsFull titles.
audit.why: The concrete driver is Flawless Duet at 16 seconds rank 1 versus Charm at a flat 12 — Ahri's answer comes back faster than Irelia's opener for the whole early game, which is exactly why the packet gives Ahri levels 6 and first item.
audit.corrected: Difficulty grounded on the 16s versus 12s cooldown comparison; pronouns fixed in every field edited.

audit.whatIsWrong: spikes[2].text refers to 'her E-reset combat pattern' and wants.you[1] says to hold Charm 'for when she commits E onto you'.
audit.why: Irelia's reset is on Bladesurge (Q). Flawless Duet (E) is a two-blade stun with a 16-second rank-1 cooldown and no reset component at all. Holding charm for the E means holding it for the ability that already stunned you.
audit.corrected: Reset re-attributed to Bladesurge in both places; wants.you[1] now says to hold Charm for the Bladesurge, not the blades.

audit.whatIsWrong: report[8].t says 'Add anti-heal early into his sustain' — vague, mis-gendered, and it never says where the sustain comes from.
audit.why: The heal is on Bladesurge itself, so it scales with how often she resets — which is why Grievous Wounds timing decides extended trades, per the missingInteractions entry.
audit.corrected: Not edited directly (report[8] is a duplicate surface), but the Bladesurge heal is now stated in tldr and dontsFull[0].d so the reader knows what the anti-heal is for.

notes: Highest-value find here is a defensive misread the page actively teaches: dontsFull[1] warned an Ahri player about Irelia's 'shielded window', but Defiant Dance reduces PHYSICAL damage only. Ahri's entire kit is magic damage plus a true-damage orb return, so W does nothing against her — poking through the charge is free, and the old text talked the reader out of it. Second correction: the reset lives on Bladesurge (Q), not on E; spikes[2].text and wants.you[1] both attributed it to E. Level chart: the full layer disagreed with the content layer and the packet on six of seven rows, including giving Irelia levels 1-3 at 7/10 while she has 600 range against a 970 orb; six side flips plus three rating corrections proposed as one atomic group, with no matching win[] edits because win[] already reads correctly. NOT WRITTEN — Vanguard's Edge carries a 'terrain: creates terrain, blocks paths and dashes' flag, and unlike the other terrain misfires in this slice Riot's own R text does describe a wall ('the blades form a wall'). But the text says only that it damages and slows enemies who walk through it, not that it blocks movement, so I did not claim it stops Spirit Rush. Whether the wall physically blocks dashes is the one thing worth checking before someone writes it.
